title: Resilience partnering field guide and activation sprint notes — 2026
content:
Purpose
Quick field guide + sprint notes for a cross-team activation to improve service reliability (surface SLOs as pragmatic commitments, run short experiments to converge on operational contracts, and seed runbooks/telemetry for scale). This is intentionally lightweight — goal: get observable, testable commitments in 6 weeks, iterate.

Context and what motivated this doc
- Multiple product teams report intermittent 95th/99th latency spikes on generation endpoints during nightly batch jobs.
- We lack a uniform signal-to-action path: alerts -> documented mitigation -> rollback or fallback.
- Product teams want predictable degradation behavior (graceful fallback to smaller-model variant / cached response).

High-level objective (North star)
- In 6 weeks, each participating service exposes 1 SLI, 1 measurable SLO (initial target), and a short contingency play that reduces customer-visible error by 50% under our simulated load profiles.

Scope (who, what)
- Core: Serving runtime + API gateway + model-caching layer.
- Teams: eng-serving-runtime (owners: Ethan, Tom), platform-engineering (Sofia), product-hosted-api (Priya), SRE (Asha + oncall rotation contributors), solutions-eng (Jorge).
- Non-goal: full org-wide SLO rollout in first iteration — we pick 3 pilot services: chat-gen, embeddings-sync, and rerank-api.

6-week activation sprint (cadence and milestones)
Week 0 (planning, kickoff): finalize service list, signal definitions, and test harness. (Owner: Asha)
Week 1: Instrument baseline SLIs (p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, success-rate for streaming chunks). Deploy lightweight dashboards. (Owner: Ethan)
Week 2: Define SLOs with product stakeholders, draft customer-impact mapping and rollback policies. Run first tabletop. (Owner: Priya)
Week 3: Implement 1st experiment: canary model-variant fallback + prefix KV-cache warmup test under synthetic spike. Run chaos/traffic test. (Owner: Tom)
Week 4: Evaluate experiment metrics, put together remediation play adjustments; author minimal runbook per service (5 steps). (Owner: Sofia)
Week 5: Run dark-launch (real traffic mirrored) to verify signal fidelity and refine alert thresholds. (Owner: Jorge)
Week 6: Final pass: communicate commitments, update oncall rotation notes, ship SLOs to monitoring and create a lightweight weekly review. (Owner: Asha)

Deliverables (each as 1-pager + artifact)
- SLI spec sheet (one per service) — measured and computed in PromQL / tracing spans
- SLO charter (target, measurement window, burn-rate action table)
- Playbook (5 bullets: detect, isolate, mitigate, rollback, postmortem owner)
- Experiment report (traffic profile, outcome, actions)
- Short enablement for oncall: checklist + 2-run scenario guide

Measurement & gating criteria
- Instrumentation gating: dashboards contain raw and aggregated SLIs within 48 hours after Week 1 deploy.
- Experiment gating: dark launch mirrors < 1% of production for first 48 hours; success if customer-visible errors drop by >= 40% in the test window.
- SLO acceptance: sign-off by product + SRE if burn-rate alerts produce documented mitigation and rollback paths.

Telemetry & alert design notes (practical heuristics)
- Prefer ratio-based SLIs (successful-response / total-requests) for error budget clarity.
- Use both rolling-window (30d) and short-window (6h) burn-rate alerts to surface fast regressions.
- Tag spans with model-variant, cache-hit, and routing-pool to enable root-cause slicing.
- Alert routing: low-severity burn-rate -> feature-team channel; high-severity -> SRE bridge and paging.

Runbook template (keep short)
1) Detection: link to dashboard + alert text
2) Quick triage: determine model-variant, pool, prefix cache-hit rate (3 checks)
3) Mitigation: (a) enable model-variant fallback OR (b) bump priority routing to dedicated pool
4) De-escalate: monitor SLIs for 30 minutes, if stable, document action and close incident
5) Postmortem: assign owner and put timeline in shared doc within 48 hours

Experiment ideas (priority order)
- Fallback variant experiment: route 5% traffic to fallback on errors, observe latency/error differential
- Cache pre-warm: on deployment, pre-warm top-500 prefixes and measure p95 shift
- Batching knob sweep: vary request batch sizes to observe throughput/latency tradeoff under sustained load

Communication plan
- Weekly short sync: 30 minutes, demo dashboards + experiment status (attendees: owners + product PMs + SRE lead)
- Daily 15m during heavy testing phases (Week 2–4) for rapid unblock
- Final readout: 1-pager to execs and a 20-min demo for engineering leadership

Risks and mitigation
- Risk: Instrumentation lag -> mitigate with synthetic checks and local trace sampling to vet metrics.
- Risk: Rollout causes noisy alerts -> prepare temporary alert-squelch scripts and a bridge runbook for squelch-with-checks.
- Risk: Cross-team scope creep -> freeze scope after Week 0; changes go through a 2-person triage (Asha + product PM).

Ops notes / quick TODOs (notes to self)
- TODO: Create synthetic workload generator (small script in infra repo) — assign to Tom (RDW-4920).
- TODO: Add model-variant tag to spans (Ethan)
- TODO: Draft SLO charter template and put in Confluence (Asha)
- Quick win: enable cache-metrics export for top-10 clients this week

Open questions
- What is an acceptable initial SLO window for streaming chat (30d rolling? 7d?): product input needed.
- Should fallback be automatic or manual for trial? (safety vs speed tradeoff)

Appendix: quick snippets and links
- Example burn-rate table: if burn-rate > 2x in 6h -> paging; >1.3x in 24h -> create incident.
- Quick query examples (PromQL-like pseudo): success_rate = sum(success{service=chat-gen}) / sum(total{service=chat-gen})
- Slack thread to post updates: #sre-reliability-sprint (use thread per service)

Next steps (this week)
- Kickoff meeting Wed 11am PT (agenda: scope freeze, test harness, owners) — calendar invite out.
- Ship Week 1 instrumentation checklist by Friday.

If anything: ping me (Asha) on Slack or drop edits directly in this doc. This is intentionally practical and experiment-first; we'll iterate based on telemetry and quick wins.
